analysis: What changed versus the 5 AM PT brief: (1) Futures firmed (NQ +0.7% vs +0.4%, SPX +0.3% vs +0.1%, Dow +0.3% vs ~flat) as the SpaceX/SMCI AI bid held into the final 30 minutes before the open. (2) Pre-bell earnings landed and the reaction pattern is harsh: Netflix -6-7% on weak Q4/ad guidance; AT&T -5-6%, ISRG -6.5%, TMO -3%, PM -2.8%, ABT -4% all fell despite beats -- guidance and one-offs are doing the moving, not the beats. (3) SMCI's raised prelim guide (+12-16%) is spreading through the AI complex: DRAM +3.5%, SOXX +2%, 3x semis ETF +4.9%, MU +~3%, NVDA +~2%. (4) NVIDIA added a second GTC Berlin leg -- Vera Rubin DSX Pods deployable in days (Barron's, single-source) -- plus quantified demand color: SpaceX flagging 200k GB300 chips/month, ~$40B financing package for Nvidia chips, AWS ~$5B upfront + ~$3B/month. (5) GOOGL (-1.1%) and MSFT (-0.25%) trail premarket on an Ireland data-center power-disclosure report (fxmag, single-source) -- grid-cost/regulatory risk for the buildout if confirmed. (6) Tonight's estimates are now pinned: Meta revenue $63.34B (+~24% YoY)/EPS ~$6.66; Tesla EPS ~$0.45 (-10% YoY)/revenue ~$27.9B (-1%); options imply META +/-10.6%, TSLA +/-6.5%. (7) 10Y ticked down 2bp to 5.10%; gold futures $4,160; BTC $83.4K (off the $81K low). Signal vs noise: futures, the morning earnings reactions, SMCI's guide, SpaceX's call numbers (SI capex $16.44B, 1.7GW compute, $1.11B/month Dec hosting deal, Q4 capex $35-40B) are confirmed; DSX Pods framing, the Ireland report, the 'can't find spare chips' line, and Ives/Munster merger odds remain single-source. USAC: nothing new -- Q3 distribution ($0.525/unit, record Oct 26) and Nov 3 earnings remain the carry-forward items.

headlines.headline: Futures firmer 30 minutes before the open: Nasdaq 100 +0.7%, S&P 500 +0.3%, Dow +0.3% (Investopedia, updated <1h ago). 10Y ticked lower to 5.10%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The SpaceX/SMCI AI bid held and firmed overnight -- but the morning's earnings-reaction pattern is 'beats aren't enough,' with several beaters selling off.

headlines.headline: Meta reports after the close today (4:30pm ET): FactSet sees revenue of $63.34B (+~24% YoY) and EPS of ~$6.66 (vs $1.05 GAAP last year; $7.25 clean of the one-time tax charge). Options imply a +/-10.6% move (TipRanks). Shares -0.4% premarket to $691.63 (finnhub, 6:08 AM PT). Wall Street will key on AI capex guidance.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest post-close catalyst today -- Meta's AI capex stance sets the tone for the whole buildout trade; the implied move says the print can swing the stock double digits either way.

headlines.headline: Tesla reports after the close (5:30pm ET): EPS est ~$0.45 (-10% YoY) on revenue ~$27.9-28.1B (-1%) (FactSet). Options imply a +/-6.5% move (TipRanks). Shares +1.6% premarket to $379.82 (finnhub, 6:08 AM PT). The print lands against the merger-committee story and Ives' $550 price-anchor math.
headlines.why_it_matters: Weak operating numbers are already priced in; the post-print conversation will be merger premium math and Musk's tone on 'not a certainty.'

headlines.headline: NVIDIA (GTC Berlin): Huang announced Vera Rubin DSX Pods -- data centers deployable in days -- and SpaceX's call flagged a 200,000 GB300 chips/month rollout plus a ~$40B financing package for Nvidia chips; AWS committed ~$5B of GB300 racks upfront plus ~$3B/month (Barron's; ad-hoc-news; Timothy Sykes summary). NVDA +~2% premarket to $220.81 (Bank of Vol).
headlines.why_it_matters: Adds a second GTC Berlin demand leg -- DSX Pods pitch Nvidia for faster enterprise deployment, and the quantified chip commitments from SpaceX/AWS keep the order-book story alive. Single-source framing, treat the framing as fragile; the premarket move is the sourced fact.

headlines.headline: Super Micro Computer surged 12-16% premarket after raising preliminary FQ1 revenue guidance to $18.5-19.5B (from $14.5-15.5B) on AI data-center demand. Memory ETF DRAM +3.5%, SOXX +2%, 3x semis ETF +4.9%; Micron +~3%, CoreWeave +3% after rebounding 1.7% Tuesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: The clearest earnings-day validation of the AI-server bid so far -- it's spreading through memory and semis, a direct read on demand rather than valuation.

headlines.headline: SpaceX follow-through: +8-9% premarket (~$159-161). Call color: $16.44B of $19.59B Q3 capex went to SI/AI, compute at 1.7GW (up from 1.4GW), a $1.11B/month hosting deal starting Dec 1 (~$13B/year), and Q4 capex guide of $35-40B. Musk said the company can't find spare AI chips even with billions to spend (single-source via Longbridge's call summary); the Tesla-merger committee story carries forward.
headlines.why_it_matters: Big quantified demand signals (capex, gigawatts, contracted revenue) are backing the premarket bid, not just merger chatter -- though ~37% of Q3 net income came from below the operating line.

headlines.headline: Alphabet and Microsoft trail premarket (GOOGL -1.1% to $336.52, MSFT -0.25% to $530.53, finnhub ~6:16 AM PT) as a report says Ireland's regulator forced disclosure of the companies' data-center power consumption. Single-source (fxmag), treat as fragile.
headlines.why_it_matters: Reads as grid-cost/regulatory risk for the AI buildout -- if more jurisdictions force power-cost pass-through, AI margins get a new headwind. The premarket weakness is sourced; the cause is not.

headlines.headline: Morning earnings reactions: Netflix -6-7% on weak Q4 revenue guide and cut 2026 ad outlook; AT&T -5-6%, Thermo Fisher -3%, Abbott -4%, Philip Morris -2.8% all fell despite beats; Intuitive Surgical -6.5% (beat, but a $450M antitrust settlement and narrowed procedure growth); United Airlines -1% (Q4 fuel warning); CME fractionally lower.
headlines.why_it_matters: The day's dominant price-action lesson: beating the quarter isn't enough -- guidance cuts, one-offs, and outlook clouds are getting punished, which frames the risk into Meta and Tesla tonight.

headlines.headline: Oil/macro into the open: WTI ~$101 (-0.7%), Brent ~$111 on Hormuz/Red Sea supply risk; API showed a 4.93M-barrel inventory draw; UK inflation came in hot at 3.5%; EIA report 7:30 AM PT and $13B 20-year Treasury auction 10 AM PT; French 10Y OAT crossed 5% for the first time since 2002.
headlines.why_it_matters: Energy stays the inflation tail risk in a 5%+ rate world -- Brent holding ~$111 keeps the lid on how far risk can rally even with an earnings bid.
